title: Require request-level committed logs alongside architecture ADRs
problem: Architecture ADRs explain long-lived technical choices but do not preserve per-request constraints, exact user wording, checks executed, and rollback links needed during incident response or support handoffs.
decision: Every delivered request is recorded in a committed request log entry (under docs/request-log) in addition to architecture ADRs, so request intent, guardrails, validation evidence, and rollback references remain auditable in-repo.
alternatives_rejected: Rely on architecture ADRs only, because they omit request-by-request execution evidence and support metadata.
Use PR descriptions/issues as the primary operational log, because they are less durable for branch-local recovery and are harder to query consistently in cloned projects.
Keep request notes outside the repository, because support and rollback responders need the same source of truth as code reviewers.
consequences: Adds lightweight documentation overhead per task, but creates a deterministic audit trail of what was asked, changed, and validated.
Improves accountability for protected areas by pairing implementation changes with explicit checks and escalation notes.
Reduces ambiguity during regression triage by preserving assumptions and must-not-change constraints with each request.
rollback_support_relationship: Request logs capture rollback_reference values that map work items to the rollback checklist and last-known-good commits/artifacts.
Support responders can quickly recover request context (scope targets, checks_run, escalation_notes) without reconstructing history from chat or PR threads.
During incidents, architecture ADRs still explain system-level intent while request logs provide transaction-level evidence for what to revert or re-run.
